name: Assign transcribed parts to pads by musical role, not spectral centroid
description:
## Why
Measured 2026-09-11 against the owner's own hand-played d14 in P03 (docs/research/reference-to-song-run.md, 'why the generated pattern was wrong'). The owner's four-on-the-floor sits on pad 2 and the backbeat on pad 3 - the pads extract_kit had labelled 'snare' and 'hat'. They picked pads by ear. Our naming (audio/kit.py: k-means on centroid/flatness/low-ratio, then lowest centroid = kick, middle = snare, highest = hat) describes the separated drum stem's spectrum, not what a part does musically, so transcribe_groove writes each part to the wrong pad even when the rhythm is right.

## Facts
- Cluster centroids on the reference clip were kick 153 Hz, snare 2287 Hz, hat 4908 Hz - a sane spectral ordering that still did not match how the owner used the pads.
- The rhythm itself was recoverable: band detection found a hit within ~10 ms of all 16 beats.
- Role is visible in the rhythm: a part on every beat is the kick, a part on beats 2 and 4 is the snare, a part on the offbeats is the hat - independent of timbre.

## Options to weigh
1. Infer role from position on the grid (periodicity and beat phase), and use timbre only to break ties.
2. Keep spectral naming but let the owner remap: return the candidate parts and their rendered previews, and take a pad assignment back.
3. Both: propose a role-based assignment and let the owner override it.

## Done when
A transcription of the 2026-09-11 reference puts the four-on-the-floor, the backbeat and the offbeat parts on the same pads the owner chose by ear, without hand-editing, and the synthetic fixture still passes. Record the rule that decided each assignment.

name: Full device access through MCP
description:
## Goal
Expose as much of the EP-133 as the protocol and file formats allow through MCP tools, so the owner can shape sounds, chop samples, set FX and mix, read and write sequencer data, and eventually import projects without Sample Tool.

## Where we stand (2026-09-11)
Proven on this hardware: GREET, STAT, FILE_INIT, METADATA_GET/SET (we only write `sym`), FILE_READ (samples + project TARs), FILE_PUT (samples). Documented upstream, untested here: FILE_DELETE, PLAY (`05 01`), GROUP_DUMP. Unknown: live project write (probing wedged the device twice upstream, once here).

## Reachable surfaces, in order of payoff / risk
1. Per-pad sound parameters via METADATA_SET (trim, playmode, envelope, pitch, level, pan, choke, stretch, midi channel) — upstream-verified, not wired up. Unlocks sound design and chopping.
2. Chopping = one upload + N pads with `sample.start/end`.
3. `fx_settings` (selector + 34 floats) and `settings` (48 floats, 4 group bytes) are carried verbatim and unmapped. Diff method maps them.
4. Velocity storage unknown (byte 4 always 100) — Dex vvg9s9ml.
5. Global settings (quantize, swing, metronome) — no known file id. STAT enumeration may find one.
6. Playing the device: PLAY command and plain MIDI notes over the same USB port.
7. Project write path — closes the Sample Tool loop. Highest payoff, highest risk; capture Sample Tool's own import before guessing.

## Rules that apply to every child
- One MIDI owner; Sample Tool counts. Every write is backup-gated (`verify_backup` current) and confirmed by the owner. Imports and experiments target a non-active project. Never commit .pak/.ppak/clips. Conventional Commits, one per piece of work.
- A hardware proof means: write, read back, power-cycle, read back again, diff a fresh backup. An ACK alone proves nothing.
- Song mode stays out of scope.

## Done when
Every child is complete or explicitly closed as not reachable with a research note under docs/research/.

name: Establish hardware baseline and backup/recovery procedure
description:
Identify connected device, OS, SKU and memory without modifying firmware. Take a full backup using a proven tool, verify archive readability and document restoration steps before any experimental write. Record a safe target pad and require explicit confirmation if occupied. Done when baseline artifacts and a usable recovery procedure exist.

Progress 2026-09-07: source audit complete; hardware procedure is docs/research/hardware-proof.md. system_profiler returned an empty USB list; no MIDI messages or writes sent. Pending: accessible EP-133, read-only identity/inventory/capacity verification, full backup and recovery baseline. Keep this task in progress until actual baseline artifacts exist.

2026-09-08 connected: EP-133 SKU TE032AS001 OS 2.0.2 responds. Read-only GREET, FILE_INIT(flags=0), root metadata and all 48 active-project pads succeeded. Sample-root metadata fileId 1000 gives capacity 62853120 and free 4096092 bytes. Active project 5; A1 sym=0. Project 1 A1 occupied. See docs/research/device-baseline.md. Pending full backup/restore baseline and sample-slot inventory; no device writes. Browser automation unavailable, user must create full Sample Tool backup.

2026-09-09: user updated firmware; read-only verification confirms OS 2.5.1, same capacity/free space, project 5 active, A1 empty. No writes. Full post-update sounds-and-projects backup remains pending. See docs/research/device-baseline.md.

2026-09-09 full backup verified: user created a full sounds-and-projects .pak on OS 2.5.1 (53,076,843 B, SHA-256 121da34a...02fb), copied outside Git to ~/Documents/ep133-backups with a .sha256 sidecar. ZIP archive, 9 project TARs + 106 WAVs + meta.json; unzip -t clean, all WAVs decode, meta.json matches SKU/OS. Sound payload accounts for 99.7% of used device memory, so the backup is complete. All 432 pads read live (read-only) and compared with the backup: 369 exact, 63 explained by slots deleted from the library, 0 unexplained.

Corrections found: metadata read nodes are numbered by project TAR pNN, NOT SysEx pad_num (hypothesis test 0 vs 118 unexplained), so physical label 1 in project 5 is node 7204, not 7207; the pad-record slot field is u16 LE at offsets 1-2, not u8; occupancy is the u32 at offsets 8-11. See docs/research/backup-verification.md.

Still open, and why this task is not complete: the RESTORE path is documented but unverified. Need the exact Sample Tool restore steps, whether restore replaces or merges the library, and whether it preserves slot ids. No writes performed.

2026-09-09 write path opened. Two authorized single-pad metadata writes (FILE_METADATA_SET {"sym":14}) succeeded, status 0, each changing exactly one of 48 pads. Node 7204 loaded physical pad "4"; node 7207 loaded physical pad "1". Combined with the 432-pad read comparison this settles pad addressing: metadata node suffix == SysEx pad_num == project TAR pNN, all one visual top-to-bottom index. The original baseline (physical 1 = node 7207) was right; an interim doc revision claiming 7204 is retracted. Upstream bug found: ep133-ppak PROTOCOL.md section 3 TAR/SysEx translation table prescribes a row reversal a Sample Tool export does not use.

Tool: tools/assign_test.py (guarded, refuses occupied pads, reversible). Pinned upstream checkout vendored at .upstream/ep133-ppak (gitignored).

Deliberately NOT reverted: project 5 nodes 7204 and 7207 currently hold slot 14. Left dirty so the restore test has a real difference to revert; restoring onto an identical device would prove nothing. Next: restore the verified .pak via Sample Tool, then re-run the 432-pad comparison and confirm both pads return to sym=0 with nothing else changed.

CORRECTION 2026-09-10: the "restore demonstrated" result is downgraded. A fresh backup diffed against the restored one shows node 7204 stored slot 14 (our write), not the backed-up 341 - the restore never reverted it. The post-restore check passed because live sym reads resolve a stale slot id to 0 while its slot is absent, which it was mid-restore. Live reads cannot verify a restore; only a post-restore backup diff can. Restore remains the recovery path but is not a proven safety net for the ACTIVE project. See docs/research/phase0-proof.md.
result: Baseline, verified full backup and a demonstrated restore all exist. Device: EP-133 SKU TE032AS001, OS 2.5.1, capacity 62,853,120 B, free 4,096,092 B, active project 5. Full sounds-and-projects .pak (SHA-256 121da34a...02fb) held outside Git at ~/Documents/ep133-backups with a sidecar; archive integrity, WAV decodability and memory accounting all check out, and it matched the live device on all 432 pads. Pad addressing settled on hardware - node suffix == SysEx pad_num == TAR pNN, physical label 1 = pad_num 7 = node 7207. name: Implement device_info and list_pads
description:
Read SKU, OS, total/free memory, unit generation when verifiable, and pad assignments across four groups. Detect capacity instead of hardcoding 64/128 MB. Report unknown values honestly and refuse writes when required capabilities cannot be verified. Done when fixture tests and real hardware output agree.

2026-09-10 handoff state: device_info is DONE and shipped in src/ep133_mcp/server.py (read-only, serial opt-in, verified through the real MCP stdio client against hardware). What remains is list_pads.

list_pads must return BOTH the resolved sym (FILE_METADATA_GET on the pad node) AND the stored slot+length from the project TAR, flagging stale references (stored slot not present in the library). The stored field is the only thing that can distinguish a truly empty pad from a stale reference - sym reads 0 for both. See docs/design/tool-contracts.md.

Blocker to resolve first: reading a project TAR live over SysEx (FILE_GET: 03 00 <project_fid u16 BE> <u32 offset 0>, then 03 01 <page u16 BE> until a short page) is documented in .upstream/ep133-ppak/ep133/project_reader.py but NOT yet verified on our hardware. Upstream warns a speculative 03 00 open on an unknown file id can wedge the device and require a power cycle - so only open known project file ids (3000 + 1000*(N-1), i.e. 3000..11000), have the owner nearby, and verify against the 2026-09-11 backup TAR byte-for-byte before trusting it. Pad record decode: slot u16 LE at offsets 1-2, length u32 LE at offsets 8-11 (verified). Done when list_pads output on hardware matches tools/diff_backups.py output for the same backup.
result: Implemented verified project TAR reader and list_pads with resolved sym, stored slot/length, labels, nodes and stale references. Known project ids only; strict page index/length checks, timeout failure, complete 48-pad TAR validation, status-based slot existence. Serialized MCP device operations. All nine live TARs byte-identical to the checksum-verified local 2026-09-11 backup; all 432 stored pad records and stale flags agree. Real MCP default-project round-trip passed (project 4, 48 pads). 231 offline tests pass; removed existing automatic hardware access from routine tests. Evidence: docs/research/project-tar-read.md. Backup verification and preflight are now ready; no writes, delete, cleanup or merge performed.

name: read_project: decode patterns, scenes, bpm and pads live from the device
description:
## What
`read_project(project, source=None)` returns the decoded project: bpm, 48 pad records, every pattern as `{group, index, bars, events:[{pad, tick, duration, note, byte7}], automation:[...]}`, scenes, and the raw `fx_settings`/`settings` floats. `source` may be a `.pak` path to decode offline instead of reading the device.

## Why
`tools/pattern_decode.py` already does all of this from a file, but only as a CLI. Exposing it over MCP lets the agent inspect what the owner played (the 77-event groove analysis in the handoff was done by hand), verify imports, and diff before/after without the owner running scripts. It is also the read half of every later FX/mix/settings mapping task.

## How
- Reuse `project_tar()` on `DeviceSession` (already used by `generate_ppak`) and the decoders in `src/ep133_mcp/protocol/patterns.py` / `projects.py`; move any logic still only in `tools/pattern_decode.py` into the package.
- Preserve type-1 (fader automation) events as a separate list; never decode them as notes.
- Read-only; no backup gate.

`read_project(1)` after the pending rebuild shows A01 with 77 events at the ticks in `YOUR-GROOVE-d14.json`; offline mode matches `pattern_decode.py` byte for byte on the fixture backups; tests green.

name: Capture and cross-check a real sample upload
description:
Using ep_133_sample_tool and authorized hardware writes, capture upload and pad-assignment traffic separately. Compare against ep133-krate and ep133-ppak; retain sanitized fixtures and command confidence notes. Done when frames, acknowledgements, transfer boundaries and assignment behavior are reproducible.

2026-09-10 upload captured and verified. 91-frame sequence (GREET, FILE_INIT flags=1, FILE_PUT_META, 87 data chunks, empty terminator) all status 0, uploaded to slots 15 and 16. Retained fixture: docs/research/fixtures/upload-capture-slot16.json (102 frames with request hex, status and response payload). Full write-up: docs/research/upload-capture.md.

FILE_INFO question RESOLVED: the terminator commits. Probing the slot between terminator and FILE_INFO in one session shows the slot already present with full metadata and free space already decremented; the later FILE_INFO returns 0 and changes nothing. upload_sample is correct; only its docstring is wrong.

Upload is bit-exact: device crc field == zlib.crc32 of local PCM (2727906176), sample.end == 18750 frames, samplerate preserved at 46875. This gives install_sample a real verification step instead of trusting an ACK.

Slot occupancy is the response status (0 = exists, 1 = "invalid file id"), never parse success; metadata records can exceed one page.

STILL OPEN for this task: cross-check the captured frames against ep133-krate captures (only ep133-ppak has been compared, by using its builders successfully on hardware). Also unexplained: 40920 bytes consumed per 37500-byte upload, reproducible but inconsistent with the backup-derived average, so preflight must re-read free space rather than predict it. Device currently holds redundant test tone in slot 15 as well as 16.

FILE_INFO resolved: the terminator commits, upload_sample is correct and only its docstring is wrong. Upload is bit-exact - device crc == zlib.crc32 of local PCM. name: Find the global settings node (quantize, swing, metronome)
description:
## What
Locate where the device stores global settings — record quantize, swing,
metronome, master volume — in the 16-bit file-id space, decode it, and expose
`device_settings()` (read) and, if writable, `set_device_settings()`.

## Why
The owner asked whether we can see the quantize setting; today the answer is
no. Nothing in the project TAR carries it (docs/research/pattern-encoding.md),
and no upstream source names a node for it. The known map is: slots 1–999,
sounds root 1000, projects root 2000, project N at 2000+1000N, pads under
that. Everything else is unexplored.

## How — read-only, owner present, fresh backup first
1. `STAT (0x0B <fid>)` is documented upstream as safe on any id. Enumerate ids
outside the known ranges (0–999 already slots; try 1001–1999, 2001–2999, and
12000+ past project 9) recording name + size for anything that answers. Go
slowly: read-only probing wedged this interface once (handoff §Open device
facts) — probably FILE_READ_OPEN on a root id, not STAT, but treat every new
id as a possible wedge and know the power-cycle recovery.
2. For any candidate node: METADATA_GET (JSON, safe) before FILE_READ.
3. Decode by the diff method: owner flips quantize on/off, agent re-reads.
4. Write `docs/research/global-settings.md` — including a negative result if
nothing answers.

## Done when

name: Record into the sequencer over MIDI
description:
## What

This would be a second write path for patterns that needs no project file and no Sample Tool: send the groove as timed MIDI, let the device record it. It also answers the quantize question from the recording side: if sent-on-tick notes come back displaced, the device quantized (or swung) them.

The note states whether MIDI-recorded events match sent timing, and what the observed quantize/swing behaviour is. Not a tool yet — a finding.

name: Calibrate band-wise drum detection against real material
description:
## Why
detector='bands' (f05bbc8) fixed the kick that the single-stream classifier missed entirely - 1 of 16 beats that all carried one - but its thresholds are guesses from one clip plus the synthetic fixture. Against the owner's hand-played bar on the same music: our hat row had 41 hits to their 8, our kick 16 to their 37. Directionally right, quantitatively wrong.

## Facts
- Constants live in audio/groove.py: BANDS, ONSET_DELTA, ONSET_FLOOR, ONSET_WAIT, LOW_DOMINANCE, HIGH_DOMINANCE. Envelopes are scaled to each band's own peak, which is why min_strength no longer thins anything under 'bands' - fix or document that too.
- tests/synth_reference.py is crude (a double-differenced-noise hat) and 'bands' does not reproduce it exactly, which is why 'classify' is still the default. Bar 1 of the fixture comes out exact; bar 2 drifts.
- The owner's d14 is ground truth for one real clip and can be read with pattern_events / pattern_steps(strict=False).

## Steps
1. Build a small calibration set: a few clips with a hand-played or otherwise trusted reference pattern, stored as patterns not audio (no copyrighted material in the repo).
2. Score detection per class (hits matched within one step, extra, missed) rather than by ear, so a threshold change is measurable.
3. Tune the constants against that score, then decide whether 'bands' can become the default and whether the fixture needs to be less crude.

## Done when
A scored comparison exists for at least one real clip and the fixture, the constants are chosen against it rather than by sweeping, and either 'bands' is the default or the reason it is not is written down.

name: Project write: import without Sample Tool
description:
## What
Learn how a project file is written to the device over SysEx, and ship `import_ppak(path, project, backup_id, confirm)` so that `generate_ppak` → import is one MCP call and Sample Tool leaves the loop.

## Why
It is the only manual step left (handoff §The one thing to know). Every sequencer, FX and mix change in this epic currently goes device → .ppak → Sample Tool by hand. Cracking this makes all of them live.

## What is known
- `FILE_PUT_META` / `FILE_PUT_DATA` are proven for samples: `02 00 05 <fid> <parent 1000> <size> <name> 00 {json}` then pages of 433 bytes.
- Project N is fid 2000+1000N and opens readable; projects root 2000 rejects with "invalid id"; sample files are named `NNN.pcm` (handoff §next real piece of work).
- Upstream: `FILE_INIT(flags=1)` + `03 00 <project_fid>` is accepted, data phase unmapped; speculative probing wedged the device twice there and read-only probing once here (PROTOCOL.md §8.3, §14.2).

## How — capture first, guess never
1. **Sniff Sample Tool.** Do not guess the payload. Run a MIDI monitor (MIDI Monitor.app, or a virtual port pass-through) while Sample Tool imports a tiny `.ppak` into a blank project. Sample Tool must be the only MIDI owner during the capture; the server stays down. Save the full frame log (never commit it — it may contain the serial). garrettjwilke's wrapper documented a MIDI-logging approach; use it as a reference for setup only.
2. Decode the capture: which fid, which parent, what name (`PNN.tar`?), what json, page size, terminator, and what STAT/finalize follows. Compare against our sample upload frames.
3. Replay against a project the rebuild blanks anyway, owner present, fresh backup, device in a state you can afford to lose. Verify with `read_project` and a post-backup diff, then power-cycle.
4. Wrap as `import_ppak` with the standard gates. Also consider whether pattern files can be written individually (a pattern is a small TAR member) — if the device accepts a partial write, `set_pattern` becomes live without rewriting the whole project.

## Done when
A generated `.ppak` imports through MCP into a non-active project, survives power-cycle, and the post-import backup diff matches the manifest `generate_ppak` predicted; `docs/research/project-write.md` records the frame layout.

name: Map fx_settings and settings by the diff method
description:
## What
Identify what each of the 34 floats in `fx_settings` (plus the selector byte)
and the 48 floats + 4 group bytes + tail in `settings` mean, by changing one
control on the device at a time and diffing backups.

## Why
Both files are present in 9/9 projects, carried verbatim by `generate_ppak`,
and modelled by nobody (docs/research/pattern-encoding.md §fx_settings,
§settings). Until they are mapped, no MCP tool can set an effect, its
parameters, or the mix. Values are n/256 floats, so a single knob turn is
unambiguous in a diff.

## How (owner at the device, agent driving)
1. Fresh `create_backup` as base. Park on a non-active project the rebuild
blanked.
2. Per step: owner changes exactly one thing (select FX type; turn one FX knob
to max; set one pad's level fader; assign the fader to a different function
for one group; toggle whatever is in settings 216–219). Agent runs
`create_backup --base` then `tools/diff_projects.py` and records `offset →
control`.
3. Selector byte: enumerate every FX type in order and note the value (0, 1,
2, 6 seen so far).
4. Write `docs/research/fx-and-settings-map.md` with a table per file: offset,
control, range, verified/probable.

## Done when
Every FX type has a selector value; every knob the owner can turn on the FX
page has an offset; the per-group fader assignment bytes are identified;
unknown remainder listed explicitly. Feeds the `generate_ppak` FX/mix task.

## Progress (2026-09-11 autonomous run)
Tooling shipped in 989b88d: protocol/diffmap.py + MCP tool diff_project(project, old, new=None) naming every changed field (live read as new, so each step is seconds). docs/research/fx-and-settings-map.md holds the nine-project survey and two hypotheses to test at the knobs: settings.params[12*g + f] = last value of fader function f for group g with group_bytes[g] the assigned function (and automation param id = the same f); fx_settings params as 17 + 17 (knob A / knob B per effect type, selector indexes the type). Step list is in the note.

name: Prove note velocity on the device so transcribed grooves keep their dynamics
description:
## Why
The 2026-09-11 hardware run got timing and pad classification right (40/43 onsets within 40 ms, median 12 ms; 8 kick / 21 snare / 14 hat matching the clusterer) and the owner still judged the groove 'nothing like the track'. Root cause measured on the reference (Above The Skyline, 16.06-23.87 s): drum onsets span a 5.9x strength range, and every hit we encode plays at ONE velocity. A break is mostly dynamics, so flattening ghost notes to accent level destroys it. min_strength (850a8d3) only thins hits; it cannot restore dynamics.

## Facts
- protocol/patterns.py writes VELOCITY_BYTE (100) into event byte 4 for every note; 'o' (SOFT_HIT) encodes identically to 'x'. VELOCITY_NOTE in protocol/generate.py states this publicly in every generate_ppak result.
- docs/research/pattern-encoding.md: event byte 4 is 100 in device-written files; whether the device honours other values is untested.
- The import ladder now passes end to end (rungs 1-4, docs/research/reference-to-song-run.md), so a velocity probe can be tested by import rather than live writes.

## Steps
1. Offline: survey event byte 4 across all 314 device-written patterns in a backup (tools/pattern_decode.py). If the device itself only ever writes 100, velocity may live elsewhere (per-pad settings, or a parameter event) - check the 5 patterns that carry the second event type (fader automation) before assuming byte 4.
2. Build a probe .ppak: one pattern, same pad, 4 hits with byte 4 = 20/60/100/127. Import into a non-active project, play, and have the owner report whether the four hits differ in level.
3. If byte 4 is velocity: map 'o' to a real value, add a velocity scale to transcribe_groove driven by onset strength, drop VELOCITY_NOTE from the results, update pattern-encoding.md.
4. If byte 4 is not velocity: record the negative result and probe the per-pad record bytes the generator currently preserves.

## Done when
Either a device-verified velocity encoding is shipped and transcribe_groove maps onset strength onto it, or a documented negative result explains where dynamics actually live. Evidence quoted as byte diffs and an owner listening report, in docs/research/.

## 2026-09-11 addendum (epic 5y8ub9um)
Now part of the full-access epic. The owner's hand-played 77-event pattern has byte 4 = 100 throughout, so velocity is not event byte 4 as the device records it. Run the capture in the same owner-at-the-device session as the fx/settings mapping: play one pad soft, then hard, into a blank pattern; `create_backup --base`; diff. If nothing in the pattern file changes, velocity may live in the pad record or be discarded on record — say which.

name: play_pad: trigger pads and slots from MCP
description:
## What
`play_pad(project, group, pad)` and `play_slot(slot)` so the agent can
audition what it installed or chopped, and the owner can hear a change without
touching the device.

## Why
Every proof today ends with "owner plays the pad and says whether it sounds
right". A trigger tool makes A/B possible during chop and set_pad work, and is
the first step toward driving the device rather than only programming it.

## Two paths, try in order
1. SysEx `PLAY`: `05 01 <fid:u16 BE> <pad bytes>` — documented upstream
(PROTOCOL.md §4) as safe, never used here. The trailing "pad bytes" are
undocumented; capture what phones24/krate send before trying. Non-destructive
by nature, but unknown payloads have wedged the interface, so owner present.
2. Plain MIDI note-on over the same USB port: the EP-133 accepts external MIDI
(groups on MIDI channels, configurable on-device; `midi.channel` is also a
per-pad metadata field). This is not SysEx and needs no protocol work — but it
does need the one-MIDI-owner rule extended so the session can send channel
messages, and the device's MIDI-in setting must be on.

## How
- Add to `DeviceSession` behind the operation lock; no backup gate (nothing
persists).
- Record which path works, latency, and whether a pad triggers with its stored
trim/pitch, in `docs/research/play-proof.md`.

## Done when
Calling the tool makes the pad sound with its stored parameters, on both an
assigned pad and a bare slot (or the note records why slots cannot be
triggered).

## Progress (2026-09-11 autonomous run)
Path 2 shipped in 667e484: DeviceSession.send_note + MCP tool play_note(channel, note, velocity, duration_s) - plain channel MIDI on the same port, under the operation lock, no backup gate. Path 1 (SysEx PLAY 05 01) checked upstream: neither phones24 nor krate implements it; krate's capture-wishlist lists audition as opcode 0x76 'completely unknown'. So PLAY needs a capture of Sample Tool auditioning a slot before anyone sends it.

Owner-present step remaining: MIDI in on, device not recording; play_note(1, 36..47) and note which pad sounds for each note on channels 1-4; try a trimmed/pitched pad to see its stored params apply; write docs/research/play-proof.md. Slots (bare, unassigned) are not reachable by channel MIDI - note that as the answer for play_slot unless PLAY gets captured.

name: set_pad: per-pad sound parameters via METADATA_SET
description:
## What
A backup-gated `set_pad(project, group, pad, params, backup_id, confirm)` that
writes any subset of: `sample.start`, `sample.end`, `sound.playmode`,
`envelope.attack`, `envelope.release`, `sound.pitch`, `sound.amplitude`,
`sound.pan`, `sound.mutegroup`, `time.mode`, `sound.bpm`, `sound.bars`,
`sound.rootnote`, `midi.channel`. Also `set_slot(slot, params)` for the
slot-level fields (name, loopstart/loopend as trim). Reads back after writing
and reports any field the device changed or dropped.

## Why
This is the largest unused surface: upstream verified the device honours these
on write (PROTOCOL.md §5–6). Our session already sends `{'sym': slot}` through
the same call (`session.py:356`). Sound design, chopping (Dex chop task) and
stretch all sit on this.

## Known rules to encode, then verify here
- Enums are strings; ints are rejected (§10.1).
- `sound.playmode` must be written with its paired `envelope.release`
(oneshot→255, key→15) or playback does not gate (§5). Auto-pair unless the
caller sets release.
- Writes are partial-merge; sending a field you did not mean to clobbers it
(§10.3). Send only what the caller asked for.
- `sound.bpm` 240 rejected; `sound.bars` clamps to powers of two.
- `loopstart/loopend` are trim-only, never auto-loop.

## How
- Contract in `docs/design/tool-contracts.md` next to install_sample: same
preflight → impact → needs_confirmation → token flow, same journal so
`undo_last_install` (or a new `undo_last_change`) can restore the previous
JSON.
- Validate ranges client-side; still trust the read-back over our validation.
- Hardware proof, owner present, non-active project, fresh backup: trim a long
sample, change pitch, set key mode, put two pads in one mute group,
power-cycle, read back, diff backup. Record in
`docs/research/pad-params-proof.md`.

## Done when
All 14 fields written and read back identically after power-cycle on at least
one pad each; undo restores; the proof note exists; tests green.

## Progress (2026-09-11 autonomous run)
Code shipped in 3adea6f: safety/params.py (ParamWriter: set_pad, set_slot, undo), DeviceSession.set_metadata, MCP tools set_pad / set_slot / undo_last_pad_change, contract entries, tests/test_params.py (439 green). Auto-pairs playmode->release, sends only requested fields, reads back and reports applied/changed/dropped/side_effects.

Blocker: MIDI port held by another session's ep133-mcp server (pid 83186) for the whole run - no hardware write attempted. Nothing observed.

Next step (port free, fresh create_backup + verify_backup -> current, non-active project): set_pad on a P03 group D kit pad (P03 is not active unless the owner moved; check device_info first): trim (sample.start/end), pitch -2, playmode key, two pads mutegroup true; read back; undo; then power-cycle with the owner and read back again. Write docs/research/pad-params-proof.md from the results.

## Progress (2026-09-12, on the device, owner power-cycled)
docs/research/pad-params-proof.md (8748de5, 8d1c9dc). A02 trim/pitch/
oneshot SURVIVED the power-cycle (5 fields verified). B02: attack,

(29): name/rootnote/bpm/bars applied. All 14 fields now written and read

to set_slot (0ecb04d). undo_last_pad_change proven on A07. Device computes

Next step: after the next cycle, read_pad(1,'B',2) -> if identical, complete.

name: chop_sample: one upload, N trimmed pads
description:
## What
`chop_sample(path, project, group, pads, slices, backup_id, confirm)` uploads
one WAV to one slot and assigns it to up to 12 pads, each with its own
`sample.start/end`. `slices` is either `{"mode":"equal","count":8}`,
`{"mode":"onsets"}` (reuse `extract_kit`'s onset detection), or explicit
`[{start_s, end_s}]`. Returns the slot, per-pad frame ranges and, for onset
mode, the detected times so the owner can adjust.

## Why
Trim lives on the pad, not the slot, so a break chopped across 12 pads costs
one slot of memory and no re-uploads. Today the only chop path is cutting WAVs
offline and installing 12 slots, which burns library space and loses the
shared source.

## How
- Compose `install_sample` (one pad gets the slot) + `set_pad` for the rest,
in one journal so undo is one step.
- Frame math at 46875 Hz mono s16; clamp `sample.end` to the file's frame
count; reject overlapping or zero-length slices.
- Offer `playmode` per chop set (default oneshot; owner may want key for gated
chops).
- Hardware proof: chop a 2-bar break 8 ways, play the pads, power-cycle, read
back.

## Done when
An 8-slice chop plays correctly from the pads, survives power-cycle, and shows
in `list_pads` with distinct trims; undo removes all 8 assignments; tests
green.

Chopper.chop/undo), MCP tools chop_sample / undo_last_chop, contract entries,
tests/test_chop.py (450 green; onset test runs on a synthetic 3-hit PCM).

the owner's power-cycle check.

## Progress (2026-09-12, on the device, owner power-cycled)
docs/research/chop-proof.md (ebd5931, 8d1c9dc). Both chops SURVIVED the
power-cycle: B02-B09 on slot 30 with eight distinct trims, D01/D02/D05 on
slot 29. undo_last_chop cleared 5/8 on hardware; the stale-prior refusal
is fixed in c638ad2 (unit-tested; this session's server predates it).
Onset mode takes the first N onsets and front-loads the chop.

Blocker: owner has not said whether the slices play right; D01/D02/D05
need a fresh server's undo_last_chop (journal adb595c9) to prove the fix.

Next step: fresh server -> undo_last_chop -> all three cleared -> owner
plays B02-B09 -> complete.

Offline 2026-09-12: pick strategy shipped (ee28a91) - first / strongest /

Owner: group D plays right, B02-B09 key mode confirmed. Found: undo_last_chop

Fixed in 1f6bbd0: Journal.records() lists newest-first; Chopper.undo takes the
first chop journal with a pad still in a revertable status and reports the
